newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases on late demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases on late demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 200 basis points at 22.00 percent on Monday. Dealers and analysts said rates fell after buyers were lured by sharp gains in rates notched up on Friday.
"Overnight rates opened under great pressure, above all due to speculation, but came down as demand returned when rates hit 24.00 percent," a fixed-income analyst said.
"Demand curbed the recent escalation in rates and the market was also awaiting the outcome of inflation data and Tuesday's primary auction," he added.

Banco de Mexico announced shortly after the close of trade on Monday that the Consumer Price Index had increased by 0.91 percent in May, the first time monthly inflation has been less than one percent since the December 1994 financial crisis.
A previously conducted Reuters survey MEX22 of 10 financial firms showed they had predicted an average rise of 0.92 percent.
The central bank will hold its weekly auction of primary government securities on Tuesday.
Traders said secondary rates also receded due to the peso halting its recent slide against the dollar.
Benchmark 48-hour contracts ended 0.25 of a centavo firmer at 7.9780/7.9825 per dollar.
"The peso held firm at 7.99 per dollar, at which rate there was no more demand for dollars," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico drained a total of 4.078 billion pesos in liquidity from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales and seven repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 150 basis points at 23.00 percent.
Dealers said forecast gains in primary rates could offset a potential downward trend in secondary rates on Tuesday in the wake of low inflation results.
Some brokers said bellwether 28-day Cetes rates could increase by 150 basis points at Tuesday night's primary auction.
Liquidity of 178 million pesos was programmed to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
